title: In vivo L4-L5 intradiscal pressure at maximal voluntary motion (Wilke 2001, one subject, re-plotted in Dreischarf 2014)
condition: in vivo, maximal voluntary flexion / extension / lateral bending / axial rotation (standing)

quantity.name: IDP
quantity.definition: absolute intradiscal pressure measured in vivo with an implanted sensor in one subject (red bars, Fig 4)

source.authors: Dreischarf M, Zander T, Shirazi-Adl A, Puttlitz CM, Adam CJ, Chen CS, Goel VK, Kiapour A, Kim YH, Labus KM, Little JP, Park WM, Wang YH, Wilke HJ, Rohlmann A, Schmidt H
source.sample: 1 subject (Wilke et al. 2001); one healthy male volunteer with L4-L5 pressure transducer (primary: Wilke H, Neef P, Hinz B, Seidel H, Claes L 2001, Clin Biomech 16 Suppl 1:S111-S126)

protocol.summary: In vivo maximal motions; FE load cases as Table 3 (flexion 1175 N + 7.5 Nm; extension 500 N + 7.5 Nm; LB 700 N + 7.8 Nm; AR 720 N + 5.5 Nm).
how_to_simulate: Apply the Table 3 combined load (compressive follower force + moment on L1)
Compare with the single-subject in vivo value
protocol.notes: In vivo, single subject, secondary. Text gives flexion 1.6 MPa explicitly; others digitised. Dreischarf discussion: 1.6 MPa corresponds to ~1900 N compression at L4-L5. Also a MSK target (msk_idp_lumbar) - do not double count with the primary Wilke 2001. Figures in the QUT eprints author version are low-resolution embedded bitmaps (~550x420 px for a 4-panel figure); digitised by pixel analysis of the extracted image against gridlines.

extraction.from: Fig 4a-d (red bars, L4-L5) and Discussion text (1.6 MPa flexion)
extraction.check_notes: Panels calibrated by frame top (2.5 or 1.2 MPa) and axis row; flexion bar 1.58-1.59 vs text 1.6. Re-read red top rows 76/90/303/298 -> 1.58/0.59/0.59/0.63.

pass_rule.rule: |model - in vivo| <= max(0.15 MPa, 25%) (template, single subject)

shared_sample_with: wilke2001: primary single-subject in vivo dataset (msk_idp_lumbar)
